description: Kobayashi Maru Override is an independent high-school student team exploring the intersection of space and technology. Our members bring a strong curiosity about space, foundational electronics skills, and hands-on experience from previous electronics projects. We use vibe coding to rapidly turn ideas into working prototypes, combining software experimentation with practical hardware knowledge. We are open to new members who are passionate about space, electronics, or building things together.
summary:
LunaWindow is an interactive web application designed to help evaluate lunar landing sites for mission planning. Users can select an existing mission location or set custom coordinates on the map and adjust the UTC time. The application displays the Sun and Earth's positions relative to the horizon and their visibility periods through a 3D lunar globe, sky view, and timeline.

Illumination, dark periods, and communication outages with Earth can be examined throughout a lunar day. Different landing sites can be compared, and results can be exported as CSV or JSON. Estimated solar energy production is calculated based on panel specifications and temperature and dust assumptions. This information supports the evaluation of potential landing sites and mission planning.

For the project, I used NASA Moon Trek and LOLA data, JPL Horizons, and published mission coordinates. The calculations are model-based estimates, not real-time surface measurements. I developed the application using Cursor, React, TypeScript, Vite, Cesium, and Astronomy Engine, configured to run locally on localhost. I used Claude Fable 5.2 and Higgsfield AI for visuals and animations, and Codex for final revisions and release preparation. LunaWindow brings astronomical data together in an interactive and accessible planning tool.
details:
LunaWindow is a web application for lunar landing-site mission planning. Users select a landing site and UTC time to see when the Sun and Earth are visible there. The application includes selected locations from Apollo, CLPS, international missions, and Artemis III candidate sites, and also allows custom coordinates to be set on the globe.

The 3D lunar globe and sky views visualize the directions of the Sun and Earth at the selected location. Throughout a lunar day, the application presents charts showing the positions of the Sun and Earth relative to the horizon, visibility windows, and times such as sunrise and sunset. Different locations can be compared, and results can be exported as CSV or JSON. Estimated energy production is also calculated using assumptions about solar panel area, efficiency, orientation, temperature, and dust. This allows users to assess potential landing sites in terms of illumination duration and the possibility of maintaining a line of sight to Earth.

The project aims to make astronomical information important for mission or landing-site planning on the Moon understandable and accessible through a single interface. NASA Moon Trek and LOLA data, JPL Horizons, and sources relating to mission locations were used in the project. The application's visibility and energy results are model-based estimates and should not be considered real-time surface measurements. When a terrain profile is loaded, the effects of the local horizon can be taken into account.

I developed the application using Cursor, React, TypeScript, and Vite. I used Cesium for 3D visualization, Astronomy Engine for calculating celestial body positions, and Tailwind CSS for interface styling. I used Claude Fable 5.2 and Higgsfield AI for animation and visual production, and Codex for final revisions and release preparation. The project was configured to run locally on localhost using the Vite development server.

LunaWindow's creative approach lies in bringing astronomical calculations together with an interactive lunar globe, sky view, timeline, and energy estimate. During development, I considered source traceability, the accurate use of location and time data, clear disclosure of estimation assumptions, and making complex data easy to compare.
